acceptance.assertion: A deterministic live audit records HTTPS redirect behavior, cache policy and the presence or absence of HSTS, nosniff, Permissions-Policy, response CSP, COOP, CORP and Referrer-Policy for representative HTML, JSON, JavaScript and CSS responses with exact URL, status and observation time.

A reviewed decision compares retaining GitHub Pages, adding a response-header-capable edge and migrating static hosting across monetary cost, privacy, operational burden, DNS, caching, deployment integrity and rollback, and selects the current no-cost retain path without overstating security.

The production delivery contract declares required mitigations, provider-unavailable headers, accepted residual risk, explicit nonclaims and re-evaluation triggers for accounts, backend writes, sensitive transactions, provider changes or new threat evidence.

Validation fails on loss of HTTPS redirect, meta CSP or declared referrer mitigation and on malformed or dishonest header evidence, while provider-unavailable response headers remain explicit measured residual-risk values rather than false failures or false positives.
Focused tests cover missing required mitigations, falsely claimed response headers, unsafe redirect targets, malformed cache or header values and unauthorized provider or DNS migration declarations.

The exact merged commit receives green required CI and a production readback whose live header matrix matches the reviewed contract; deviations fail closed and do not silently rewrite the accepted boundary.

No DNS, hosting-provider, edge-routing, credential or paid-service mutation occurs; rollback is deletion of the new contract and readback enforcement while preserving the existing GitHub Pages deployment.

Closeout binds base, head, full UTF-8 diff, self-review, any external review, green CI, merge commit and live readback, and registers any unimplemented edge or migration work as a separate future task.

approval.note: Implement only the reviewed no-cost retain-GitHub-Pages decision and its machine-readable header contract, validator, tests and production readback. Do not change DNS, provider, edge routing or incur costs without a separate reviewed authorization.

goal: Re-evaluate and implement Commonworld's HTTP response security-header boundary by retaining the current cost-free GitHub Pages delivery for the static account-free product, recording the accepted provider-bound residual risk, and adding exact machine-readable contracts, tests and live readback without changing DNS or hosting.

does_not_establish: permission to add a paid edge provider
that meta CSP is equivalent to response-level CSP

rollback.strategy: Revert the contract, validator, tests and workflow integration while leaving the existing GitHub Pages deployment, DNS and static artifacts unchanged.

title: Make the HTTP response security-header boundary explicit
